packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-04 - unverified image reading

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- No proposed identification of the work or text was in my context. My standing context did contain a project note mentioning a "Stams pilot" for a fragment-identification project, and the task directory is named "stams-b1-readers"; the overviews also show a pencilled shelf note at the foot of the leaf (image-001 and image-005, below the text block, roughly "Stams, StA, Frg. 18?" - last digits uncertain). That concerns the holding, not the work. I did not use it.
- Beyond the rules: I listed the two packet directories to get the image filenames, and made contrast-enhanced crops (in my scratch directory) of the faded lines in image-003 and image-007 to read them. Nothing else opened.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Two overviews: image-001 (one face, tiles image-002..004) and image-005 (other face, tiles image-006..008). Single leaf, upper corners cut off, punched hole at top centre, fold/crease across the middle; lower margin folded over.
- Single column. Red-ruled staff lines (dry-point/red lines), each text line preceded by a row of unheighted/heighted neumes (German-type neumes on red lines). Clef letters at the left of neume rows: "f" on the image-001 face, "c" on the image-005 face. Small check marks at the right margin of several neume rows.
- Rubrication: red "R" (responsory sign) and "V" (verse sign) before enlarged red or ink-and-red initials (D, M, C, D, T, T, I, A). Red wavy/strokes fill gaps in text where melismas extend. Vertical red bar lines in the neume rows.
- Image-005 face: roman numeral "LVI" at top centre (folio number?). 
- Interpretation (tentative): chant book with noted responsories and verses; no commentary or glosses.
- Middle of image-001 face (text lines around the "Cum" initial) and middle of image-005 face (two lines) are badly faded/abraded.

LINE CONVENTION: only text lines are numbered, counted from the top of each tile; neume rows are not transcribed. Tiles overlap by one text line; overlaps noted. "|" not used; red elements marked [red]. ~ = red filler stroke in a melisma gap.
